notes.title: Improved Understanding & Some Explanations
notes.content:
This update aims to improve clarity around certain in-game elements. We’ve hidden key information behind spoiler tags to preserve the experience for new players. But if you’ve already finished the game or watched playthroughs on YouTube, Twitch, etc., feel free to read on without worry.
[list]
[*] Some players were confused by the man’s dialogue at the end of the game. We’ve slightly adjusted the final cutscene to make its meaning clearer.

Explanation:
[spoiler][b]Q:[/b] What the hell? Why does this guy want to take my legs?
[b]A:[/b] Well, the game doesn't have a negative meaning, although it's not a happy ending.
The meaning is actually quite simple. Our nameless hero survived the nightmare, but after repeatedly bashing his knees against walls and pillars, they’re probably ruined. That’s all the man is referring to at the end. But are his knees really destroyed, or is that man lying? That’s a story for another time..[/spoiler]

[*] Some players didn't understand the purpose of the empty security room on the 8th floor, so this gameplay moment has also been reworked for better understanding.

Explanation:
[spoiler][b]Q:[/b] What's the point of this room? I just wasted my time.
[b]A:[/b] Again, the explanation is straightforward. The little girl stole a gun from the security room, hid it on the 2nd floor, and in return asks the player to find her toy. This is hinted at by an alternate game path — a gun can be found in the locked security room on the 6th floor.[/spoiler]

[*] Minor adjustments to difficulty levels.
[/list]
Best Regards,
Ells&Pills

notes.title: Difficulty Selection
notes.content:
This small update adds a difficulty selection screen. It’s very challenging to please all players, as all players are different. There are casual gamers, there are hardcore gamers, and everyone has different levels of patience.

As a result, we have created three difficulty levels:
[list]
[*] Easy. At this difficulty level, the stability of the chair is increased by 2 times. You would have to intentionally do something foolish for the chair to tip over during the descent..
[*] Normal. The chair's stability remains unchanged from what it was before this update.
[*] Hard. The chair's stability has been returned to approximate values as it was at the game's release. This is the original, classic version of the game.
[/list]
We hope that now most of you will find a difficulty level that you consider suitable. Take care of your knees! ;)

Best Regards,
Ells&Pills

notes.title: Partial Controller Support
notes.content:
This small update adds partial controller support, the game has been tested on the original Xbox 360 controller.

[b]An important note:[/b] [u]we develop games with a focus on keyboard and mouse, so the support is only partial. Specifically, the controller does not work in the menu because it is designed for mouse cursor navigation.[/u] It is possible that for our future games, we will redesign our menu to equally support both keyboard and mouse as well as controllers.

[b]Button Layout:[/b]
[list]
[*] LMB = Left Trigger
[*] RMB = Right Trigger
[*] Q = Left Shoulder
[*] E = Right Shoulder
[*] WASD = D-Pad
[*] Camera = Right Thumbstick
[*] Hold R = Hold B
[*] Spacebar = Left Shoulder (bonus game mode)
[*] F = Right Shoulder (bonus game mode)
[*] M = A (bonus game mode)
[*] Escape = Back
[/list]
Controller vibration has also been added for collisions and hits. It’s possible that some of you may find it more convenient to play with a controller instead of a keyboard and mouse.

Best Regards,
Ells&Pills

notes.title: Additional Branch for Physics Testing
notes.content:
Hello!

Before the game’s release, the only rare and critical issue we found was the incorrect setting of the game window resolution on the first launch. After the release, it turned out that the game’s most important feature is also malfunctioning for some players. Moreover, the problem affects not only players with low-end PCs but also some users with powerful, modern machines.

If the game indeed runs incorrectly on PCs below the minimum system requirements, it’s likely because those PCs can’t keep up with all the physics and collision calculations. However, the situation with high-end PCs is unclear. We suspect that the PhysX game engine might not work properly on RTX 5000 series graphics cards. Although, this issue supposedly only affects very old games that are many years old.

We’ve added an additional branch with a separate game build where the physics behavior has been slightly modified. You can switch to this branch in the game’s Properties within the Steam client. If you’re experiencing physics issues like chairs flipping over for no reason, please try the build from this additional branch. And let us know if anything changes.

Best Regards,
Ells&Pills

notes.title: Adjustment of Chair Stability and Camera Shake
notes.content:
Thank you very much for the feedback you share! <3

This small but important update includes the following changes:
[list]
[*] We have slightly adjusted the chair’s stability, so it should tip over much less often now. However, you still need to be careful when going down stairways — it’s not a walk in the park!
[*] Additionally, we have added an option in the settings to reduce camera shake. The effect of this option is subtle but makes things a bit easier.
[/list]
The game features two types of camera shake. The first is the shake caused by the character’s animations — the camera is attached to the character’s head and moves synchronously with it. This effect is difficult to remove as it happens naturally.
The second is an additional fake camera shake that activates when pressing the WASD keys. Thanks to the new option, this shake can now be disabled.

Best Regards,
Ells&Pills

notes.title: I'm still strapped to a rolling office chair with a ticking timer in a huge scary building
notes.content:
Beware minor spoilers for Chairbound in this piece. I think they're minor. I have no idea what's truly significant in this dreary purgatory of flourescent lights and rippled glass facades. Only one thing seems guaranteed: I have to get out of here in 10 minutes or I'm doomed.

I met the weird little girl again. She was loitering in the shadow of a pillar on the eighth floor. I found her goblin-esque during our first meeting, but up close she seems relatively ordinary, a pale 10-year-old in a nightie with shoulder-length hair. At least, until she burbles distorted sounds at me and runs away into the darkness. I gather she is looking for her "toy". I don't think it's the rubber duck I'm holding.

After almost a year, we’re excited to announce the upcoming release of the new game [b]Ells Tales[/b], returning to the roots of the series! Missing the separate control of each of the character’s hands and that retro-style graphics?

So, we’re proud to present the new chapter — [b]Ells Tales: Chairbound[/b]. Step into the shoes of a person tied to an office chair in the middle of a gloomy office building. Control the movement and rotation of the chair using physics, but be careful not to tip over, and find your way to escape before time runs out!
